name: Tri
description: The spitter, drawn alone and on no frame of Dot's: the belly changed all of it. Tri let the hive's work be done on it so it could throw acid, and the body is the price. The belly is swollen into a sac wider than the chest, and over it Tri wears a white gown — the one it was worked on in, loose from the shoulders to the knees, pushed forward by the sac so the front hem rides up, creased where the cloth pulls over a belly that hangs like a drop, heaviest low and sagging over the hips, and stained with acid down the front, across the belly and spattered at the hem. Everything above the hips is thrown back to balance the weight, and the arms hang out from the sides in loose sleeves to the elbow, the forearms and hands bare. Below the hem the legs are bare and swollen from the knee down — the calves thick, the ankles gone, the feet puffed up round the straps of a pair of plain sandals. Nothing is carried but the dead organ on its cord above the belly. The head is `ss.lib.tri-head` composed at a quarter of its size, tilted back with the chin up: a white hood with the goggles worn down over the eyes, the face whole and lumped with tumours like the forearms and the legs, the mouth uncovered and stained at the corner where the acid comes out, a throat swollen into a gland under the jaw. No feelers — those are Dot's weapon. It stands back on its heels and breathes with the belly, and it walks in a slow lurch. Drawn facing +x; the game flips it.

idle.description: thrown back on the heels with the belly forward: the sac does the breathing, a slow swell under the gown that lifts the whole front; the chest rocks a hair behind it, the head lifts on the in-breath, and the arms, held out from the belly because they cannot hang straight, drift out and back

walk.description: a slow lurch: short steps on the swollen legs, the sandals slapping down with a heavy drop as each lands, the upper body rolling forward and back over the hips a beat behind the feet and the belly a beat behind that, the gown swinging with it, the head nodding, the arms swung wide and loose for balance
